title: Finite scheme quotients for admissible locally finite-type actions over a field
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $V$ be a separated scheme locally of finite type over $e$ [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let a finite group $H$ act by $e$-scheme automorphisms. Suppose every orbit of underlying points is contained in an affine open of $V$. Then there are an $e$-scheme $Q$ and a finite surjective invariant $e$-morphism $q:V\to Q$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Its geometric fibres are the $H$-orbits [def-weil-geometric-fibre], its underlying map is a topological quotient, and for every open $U\subseteq Q$, the canonical map identifies $\mathcal O_Q(U)$ with $\mathcal O_V(q^{-1}U)^H$. Every invariant morphism from $V$ to a scheme factors uniquely through $q$. On an invariant affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$, the quotient is $\operatorname{Spec}(R^H)$. The scheme $Q$ is locally of finite type over $e$ and is reduced if $V$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The quotient restricts to invariant opens. If $v:V\to B$ is an invariant $e$-morphism and $v^{-1}U\to U$ is finite for an open $U\subseteq B$, then $Q\times_B U\to U$ is finite. Every action on a quasi-projective finite-type $e$-scheme satisfies the orbit-in-an-affine hypothesis, as does every subgroup action. Quasi-projective means a locally closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over $e$ [def-kun-projective]. No faithfulness, freeness, tameness or quasi-compactness of $V$ is required, and no projectivity of $Q$ is asserted.

proof.text: Intersect all translates of an affine neighbourhood of each orbit. Separated affine intersections give an invariant affine cover. On $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ use the action groupoid $\coprod_H W\rightrightarrows W$: source $(h,x)\mapsto x$, target $(h,x)\mapsto hx$, inverse $(h,x)\mapsto(h^{-1},hx)$, composition $(g,hx)(h,x)=(gh,x)$. The finite coproduct is $\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_H R)$; its source has the coordinate module basis, hence is finite locally free, and inversion identifies target with source. The groupoid orbit lemma gives ordinary and algebraically closed-point orbit fibres over $\operatorname{Spec}(R^H)$ and surjectivity. Integrality makes this map closed, hence a topological quotient.

source.place: Tag 03BL, lemma-points; finite free action groupoid via 02KB; integrality 0BRI and closedness 00GU/00HZ

proof.text: Apply the orbit ringed-space lemma to form $Q=(|V|/H,\mathcal F)$, with invariant-section sheaf and open orbit map $q$. Each invariant affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is saturated. Step 1 identifies $q(W)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R^H)$ topologically; the fixed-endomorphism sheaf lemma identifies their sheaves by the canonical inclusion. These are affine charts, so $Q$ is a scheme and $q|_W$ is the usual spectrum morphism, local on stalks. The invariant structure morphism $V\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ factors through $Q$, giving its $e$-structure. The same lemma gives the categorical quotient and restriction to every invariant open.

source.place: IX 1.4, pp.132--133, admissible quotient; explicit orbit-space and invariant-sheaf construction supplied here

proof.text: The affine-cover criterion makes $q$ affine. On any affine $T=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Q$, write $q^{-1}T=\operatorname{Spec}R$; then $A=R^H$. The affine-pairs criterion gives $R$ finite type over $e$. Apply the invariant-subalgebra lemma: $R$ is finite over $A$, $A$ is finite type over $e$, and $A$ is reduced if $R$ is. The definitions give finiteness of $q$, local finite type of $Q$, and reducedness when $V$ is reduced. Step 1 gives surjectivity and geometric orbit fibres globally.

source.place: Tag 02JJ, lemma-characterize-finite-in-terms-of-integral (3) => (1), with lemma-characterize-integral; integrality 0BRI; affine-pairs criterion Morphisms 01T2, affine criterion 01S8

proof.text: Let $b:Q\to B$ factor $v$. For affine $T=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq U$, finiteness of $v$ gives invariant affine $v^{-1}T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ finite over $C$; its quotient is $b^{-1}T=\operatorname{Spec}(R^H)$. The affine-pairs criterion gives $R$ finite type over $e$. The arbitrary-base clause of the invariant-subalgebra lemma makes $R^H$ finite over $C$. Thus $b^{-1}U=Q\times_B U\to U$ is finite.

proof.text: For quasi-projective $V$, factor its immersion into projective space as a closed immersion into an open. Apply the Proj finite-set lemma to every finite orbit. Every subgroup orbit is contained in a whole-group orbit, so the same affine neighbourhood works.

lean.statement: theorem exists_admissible_finite_type_field_quotient (e : Type u) [Field e] (V : Scheme.{u}) (p : V ⟶ Spec (.of e)) [IsSeparated p] [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (H : Type v) [Group H] [Finite H] (a : H →* Aut V) (ha : ∀ g : H, (a g).hom ≫ p = p) (horbit : ∀ x : V, ∃ W : V.affineOpens, ∀ g : H, (a g).hom x ∈ W.1) : ∃ (Q : Scheme.{u}) (b : Q ⟶ Spec (.of e)) (q : V ⟶ Q), q ≫ b = p ∧ IsAdmissibleFiniteSchemeQuotient a q ∧ Surjective q ∧ (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Q), Nonempty ↥(pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) q t) ∧ ∀ x y : ↥(pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) q t), ∃ (g : H) (l : pullback q t ⟶ pullback q t), l ≫ pullback.fst q t = pullback.fst q t ≫ (a g).hom ∧ l ≫ pullback.snd q t = pullback.snd q t ∧ l x = y) ∧ (∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : V ⟶ Z), (∀ g : H, (a g).hom ≫ f = f) → ∃! r : Q ⟶ Z, q ≫ r = f) ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType b ∧ (IsReduced V → IsReduced Q) ∧ (∀ W : V.Opens, (∀ g : H, (a g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ W = W) → ∃ (O : Q.Opens) (aW : H →* Aut W.toScheme) (r : W.toScheme ⟶ O.toScheme), q ⁻¹ᵁ O = W ∧ (∀ g : H, (aW g).hom ≫ W.ι = W.ι ≫ (a g).hom) ∧ r ≫ O.ι = W.ι ≫ q ∧ IsAdmissibleFiniteSchemeQuotient aW r ∧ ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : W.toScheme ⟶ Z), (∀ g : H, (aW g).hom ≫ f = f) → ∃! s : O.toScheme ⟶ Z, r ≫ s = f) ∧ (∀ (W : V.Opens) (hW : IsAffineOpen W), (∀ g : H, (a g).hom ⁻¹ᵁ W = W) → ∃ (O : Q.Opens) (hpre : q ⁻¹ᵁ O = W) (_ : IsAffineOpen O) (i : O.toScheme ≅ Spec (.of (finiteQuotientInvariantSections a W))), q.resLE O W (le_of_eq hpre.symm) ≫ i.hom = hW.isoSpec.hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (finiteQuotientInvariantSections a W).subtype)) ∧ ∀ (B : Scheme.{u}) (c : B ⟶ Spec (.of e)) (v : V ⟶ B), v ≫ c = p → (∀ g : H, (a g).hom ≫ v = v) → ∃ r : Q ⟶ B, q ≫ r = v ∧ r ≫ c = b ∧ ∀ U : B.Opens, IsFinite (v ∣_ U) → IsFinite (pullback.snd r U.ι)
